Ti–O solid–gas thermodynamics

Calculate oxide phase stability, vacancy distribution within a particle, and isolated-vacancy loss during pretreatment.

Vacancy distribution

Calculate the equilibrium distribution of a measured oxygen-vacancy concentration among surface, subsurface and bulk sites in rutile at 600 °C. Use the calculated reactive-site concentration to estimate the apparent CO turnover frequency (TOF).

Method

The measured oxygen removal sets the total vacancy concentration in each sample. The model distributes these vacancies and their associated electrons among rutile sites by minimising the free energy at 873.15 K (600 °C). The total vacancy concentration remains fixed. Calculations cover 720 parameter combinations and five definitions of a reactive site.

Site capacities

Particles are represented as smooth spheres of diameter D, with density ρ = 4.2487 g cm⁻³ and molar mass M = 79.866 g mol⁻¹. Site capacities are expressed in µmol per gram of initial TiO2.

Am=6ρD,A110=2ac,cBRI=AmA110NACk,i=f110micBRI(1−zk,iR)2,mBRI=1,mIPL=2,mSBR=1,mTi=2CO,tot=2×106M,CTi,tot=106M

k = 1–4 is the trilayer, zk,i the depth of site i (a = 0.4594 nm, c = 0.2958 nm, O parameter u = 0.30479). O and Ti below the trilayers are the remainder of CO,tot and CTi,tot, split over 240 bulk shells by volume. Each site is counted once.

State table and free energy

Each group of equivalent cells, d, has a concentration Cd (µmol g⁻¹). A cell in state a has energy Eda, degeneracy gda, vda O vacancies and eda Ti3+. Populations xda = Cdpda minimise

F=∑d,axdaEda+kBT∑d,axdalnxdaCdgda+12∑ℓ,mqℓHℓmqm

at T = 873.15 K, subject to

∑axda=Cd,∑d,avdaxda=NV,∑d,aedaxda=2NV

NV: measured O removal of the sample (µmol O g⁻¹).

Vacancy segregation energies

BRI denotes bridging oxygen, IPL in-plane oxygen, and SBR subbridging oxygen.

Single-vacancy formation energies are expressed relative to bulk, εk,i = Ef,k,i − Ef,bulk, using one of four energy sets: Pabisiak and Kiejna (2007, GGA; PAB)1, Hameeuw et al. (2006, LDA; HAM)2, or Li et al. (2015, screened-exchange; LI_SBR1 and LI_L2)3. LI_SBR1 assigns the Li subsurface energy to layer-1 subbridging sites; LI_L2 assigns it to all layer-2 oxygen sites. Sites not specified in the selected energy set are assigned the bulk value (ε = 0). For the Li sets, ε1,IPL = ε1,BRI + 0.11 eV 4. Individual oxygen sites have occupied and vacant states:

E∈{0,εk,i},v∈{0,1}

(1×2) cell and reconstruction

Each cell contains two bridging oxygen sites and the four Ti sites beneath them in layer 1, giving Ccell = CTi,1/4. For each oxygen configuration, n electrons can occupy the remaining Ti sites as Ti3+ polarons, at an energy s0 = 0.2 eV per electron5:

E=Eo+ns0,g=go(nfreen),e=eo+noEoveogo (nfree)intact0001 (4)one vacantε1,BRI102 (4)both vacant2ε1,BRI201 (4)reconstructedε1,BRI+ΔG121 (2)

ΔG is relative to the one-vacancy state. Reconstructed fraction of bridging sites and vacant fraction of the unreconstructed ones:

frec=2xrecCBRI,θ=NV,BRICBRI−2xrec

Bulk aggregates

Bulk oxygen sites below 1.30 nm are represented by periodic boxes containing 700 sites (5×5×7 cells). Configurations with N vacancies contribute to the partition function Q(N), which gives the free energy EN:

EN=−kBTlnQ(N),vN=N,0≤N≤175Q(N)=∑σ∈ΩNexp(−1kBT∑i<j,rij≤rcJ(rij)σiσj)J(r)=Ar−Br2−Cr6,A=0.753,B=11.83,C=−383.45

J is the bulk vacancy-pair interaction energy6 (r in Å, J in eV), and rc is the cutoff distance. Cluster interaction energies are calculated as sums of pair energies. ΩN contains configurations with N vacancies, each associated with two Ti3+ among its three Ti neighbours, with at most one electron per Ti7. Q(N) is calculated by Monte Carlo sampling and Widom insertion over all sites available for vacancy insertion:

Q(N+1)Q(N)=⟨W⟩NN+1,W=∑i emptyexp(−hikBT)

hi: pair energy of site i with the present vacancies. Boxes do not interact.

Charge

State charge z = 2v − e (elementary charges). Each atomic plane is a spherical shell ℓ of radius rℓ with charge qℓ. Shells can carry charge while the total particle charge remains zero.

qℓ=∑(d,a)∈ℓzdaxda,∑ℓqℓ=0ϕℓ=∑mHℓmqm,Hℓm=κεrmax(rℓ,rm)mpNA10−6,κ=1.43996 eVnm

εr = 64 (a axis) or 107 (c axis), rutile at 873 K8. mp: particle mass (g).

Equilibrium populations

The equilibrium state probabilities have the Gibbs form, with multipliers μV (vacancy), μe (electron) and the shell potentials φℓ:

pda=gdaZdexp[−Eda+zdaϕℓ(d)−μVvda−μeedakBT],Zd=∑a(⋯)

The multipliers minimise the convex dual (β = 1/kBT, u = βφ, fda = (v, e, −z)):

Ψ(y)=∑dCdlnZd(y)−bTy+12uT(βH)−1u∇2Ψ=∑dCd[⟨ffT⟩d−⟨f⟩d⟨f⟩dT]+blkdiag(0,(βH)−1)

by damped Newton steps. (βH)−1 is tridiagonal (nested spherical capacitors), so a step costs O(shells). The start is the solution with every trilayer and bulk shell neutral, the εr → 0 limit.

Equal-mass mixture over D = 900, 1133, 1367, 1600 nm, each at the same NV per gram:

Limits

Equilibrium at 600 °C with complete transport; pretreatment kinetics and cooling are not modelled. Samples treated at ≥ 900 °C (R1000, R1100) are in the regime where Ti2O3-(1×2) is reported9.

Validation

Model tests (pilot/titania-super-multiscale/tests): each O and Ti site counted once; Monte Carlo box free energy exact for N = 1, 2 and seed-independent at N = 170 (0.05 eV per vacancy); inventory, charge neutrality and Poisson residuals; analytic gradient and Hessian against finite differences; scalar μ, μe limit at large ε, deviation ∝ 1/ε; Debye–Hückel screening length; reconstruction fraction → 0 at ΔG = 5 eV; stored results regenerate.

Method

Scope. C–H–O–N / Ti–O Gibbs equilibrium. Gas registry in this version: CO2, H2, CO, H2O, N2, O2. Hydrocarbon species (CH4), graphite, nitrides, and the rutile TiO2−x solution phase are not included in this version. The calculation is a closed, finite-inventory equilibrium between one gas charge and one solid charge, not a flow-reactor steady state. Every reported value is gibbs_min.

Gas-phase RWGS atlas

The atlas first removes the solid from the question. For a fresh H2/CO2 feed it solves the single equilibrium

CO2+H2⇌CO+H2O

on a one-mole fresh-gas basis. Because the reaction has no net change in gas moles, this ideal-gas conversion ceiling is independent of total pressure. The separate gas–solid curve then uses the oxide mass, gas charge, pressure, and volume from the input panel. A difference between the two curves means oxygen exchange with the solid has entered the equilibrium result.

Finite gas–solid contact

The solver computes the minimum of the total Gibbs energy

G=∑i∈gasniμi+∑j∈solidmjμj∘(T)μi=μi∘(T)+RTln(yiPP∘)

subject to the elemental balance 𝐀𝐳=𝐛 and 𝐳≥0, where 𝐳 collects all gas and solid amounts. Gases form an ideal mixture; each condensed phase is a pure line compound at unit activity. The inputs defining b are the initial gas composition, the gas charge ng,0=PV/(RTcharge), and the initial solid phase and mass. The equilibrium phase split is an output.

min𝐳≥0G(𝐳;T,P),𝐀𝐳=𝐛yi=ni∑k∈gasnkbe=∑i∈gasaieni+∑j∈solidajemj

Amounts are in mol; standard chemical potentials are per mole of the species or solid formula unit. aie is the number of atoms of element e in species i. The gas constant and chemical potentials must use the same energy unit, and P/P∘ is dimensionless.

Active set. Condensed phases are enumerated as candidates: every single phase and every phase pair (the phase rule allows two line compounds in an M–O system at fixed T and P; N2 adds no solid component). For each candidate the equilibrium conditions are

μi=∑eaieλe(i∈gas)μj∘=tjλTi+ojλO(j∈active solids)

solved by Newton iteration in the element potentials λ with the gas in logarithmic coordinates. Condensed amounts follow linearly from the Ti and O balances through the combination O − ρhost·Ti, which removes the host oxygen symbolically; coexisting phases are resolved down to ~10−41 mol. A phase outside the candidate is not a variable and is exactly zero in the result.

Stability criterion. Each inactive phase carries a reduced cost rj = μ°j − tjλTi − ojλO, reported per formula unit and per mole of oxygen (defj = 2tj − oj; defj = 1 for each TiO2→Magnéli step). The problem is convex, so a feasible candidate with all rj ≥ 0 is the global minimum. Candidates are not ranked by total Gibbs energy, whose differences can fall below double-precision resolution. Reduced costs at zero within tolerance are reported as phase coexistence.

Phase stability and iteration

Element potentials enforce atom conservation. Differentiating the constrained Gibbs energy gives the gas equilibrium conditions above and the solid-phase reduced costs:

ℒ=G−λT(𝐀𝐳−𝐛)rj=μj∘−tjλTi−ojλOmj≥0,rj≥0,mjrj=0

A phase present at equilibrium has zero reduced cost. A positive reduced cost means that adding an infinitesimal amount of that phase raises the constrained Gibbs energy. For reduced titanium oxides, the plotted oxygen-normalized value is

Δj=2tj−oj,rj,O=rjΔj(Δj>0)

Each candidate phase set is solved iteratively. With the balance and equilibrium equations collected in 𝐅, the Newton correction satisfies

𝐉(𝐮k)Δ𝐮k=−𝐅(𝐮k)𝐮k+1=𝐮k+αkΔ𝐮k,0<αk≤1

Here 𝐉 is the Jacobian, 𝐮 contains the solver coordinates, and αk controls the step length. The iteration stops when the equilibrium equations and atom balances meet the numerical tolerance; the remaining phases are then checked for stability.

Oxygen-free feeds. Under pure H2 or N2 the single-phase candidate leaves the gas with zero oxygen inventory, and the derivative of G toward forming a trace of O-bearing gas together with a reduced phase diverges. The solver therefore reports the two-phase buffer with a finite trace amount; under sealed N2 this trace is the equilibrium result. An O2 impurity at the ppm level is sufficient to suppress reduction, with a positive margin.

The oxygen-potential margin used by earlier versions of this site equals the reduced cost per mole of oxygen (the dual of the same minimisation); it is reported in the phase-stability checks below. Independent verification is provided by an 80-digit reference implementation and by the NIST–Waldner data comparison in the validation section below.

Method

The titration gives the total oxygen removed per sample. The model splits it into three populations,

nV,tot=niso+nassoc+nbelow

Removal is generated uniformly over the reduction time, g=nV,tot/tred. A new vacancy joins the surface active region of capacity ns with probability ffree=1−(niso+nassoc)/ns and otherwise goes below it. Two isolated vacancies associate at second order.

g=nV,tottred,q=niso+nassocffree=1−qns

Population balances

dnisodt=gffree−2klossnsniso2dnassocdt=2klossnsniso2dnbelowdt=g(1−ffree)

All three populations start at zero. Associated vacancies are counted as vacancies, rather than as pairs, so association transfers equal amounts between the first two populations. Summing the balances gives

ddt(niso+nassoc+nbelow)=gniso(t)+nassoc(t)+nbelow(t)=gt

Reduction to one equation. With q=niso+nassoc the loss term cancels from the sum:

dqdt=g(1−qns)q(t)=ns[1−exp(−gtns)]nbelow(t)=gt−q(t)

Thus ffree=exp(−gt/ns), and a single scalar equation remains:

dnisodt=gexp(−gtns)−2klossnsniso2niso(0)=0kloss=νeffexp(−ElosskBT)nassoc=q−niso

At t=tred, the sum of the three populations equals the measured total inventory. Populations and capacity use µmol O g⁻¹, time uses s, g uses µmol O g⁻¹ s⁻¹, and kloss and νeff use s⁻¹. Eloss and kBT use eV. The scalar equation goes to an implicit integrator (Radau in the package, Strang splitting in the browser), which stays stable wherever a parameter search tries a small Eloss with a large νeff.

Rate. The initial CO formation rate is taken proportional to niso with one coefficient for every sample; rates are compared as ratios normalised to R600.

rCO(sample)rCO(R600)=niso(sample)niso(R600)

Fit. Three parameters, ns (bounded between the bridging row and the bridging row plus the first subsurface oxygen layer, 13.6 to 67.8 µmol-O g⁻¹), Eloss and log10 νeff, against five rates. The rates span 86-fold, so the residual definition moves the fit: a log or relative residual recovers the reported parameters, a raw residual is dominated by one sample.

Inputs and limits. niso is inferred from the measured rates. The rates constrain niso; nassoc and nbelow follow from the assumed second-order loss law, uniform generation and constant capacity ns. Surface area is held constant through the 1000 °C treatment (sample BET values unavailable). The model contains no reconstruction, cluster geometry or shear structure. Eloss and log νeff are effective parameters of the net isolated-vacancy loss rate constant kloss.

Numerical fit

Browser against package

The browser integrates the same scalar equation as the Python package with a different integrator, Strang splitting against Radau, and a parity gate holds the two to a relative 1e−6 across the reduction series and the parameter search. The reported parameters reproduce the supplement's table at the reported digits.
